assessment: KdpFABC is a bacterial potassium uptake transporter made up of a channel-like subunit (KdpA) and a P-type ATPase (KdpB). When potassium levels are low (< 2 mM), the transporter actively and selectively uptakes potassium, but must be switched off again to prevent excessive potassium accumulation. Here, by using cryo-EM, pulsed EPR measurements and MD simulations the molecular basis KdpFABC for inhibition by phosphorylation has been defined to an arrested (off-state) that is in a distinct conformation from previously determined P-type ATPase structures.
